# Bug 165 — a runtime call generated by Elab binds to a same-named function the module defines

**Status:** OPEN
**Found:** 2026-10-22, by the Codex review (round 4) of the symbol-name work (bug 129, branch `symbols`).
**Severity:** silent wrong code in safe code. `println(x)` is desugared by Elab into calls spelled
`print_int` / `print_char` / `print_string` / `print_bool`, and those calls bind by spelling. A
module that defines its own function under one of those names gets it called by every `println`
and `print` in that module, instead of the runtime helper. No `extern`, no `trusted` needed.

## Reproducer

`tests/regressions/bug165_generated_helper_call_binds_by_spelling/repro.con`:

```con
mod m {
    fn print_int(x: Int) with(Process) {
        abort();
    }
    pub fn main() with(Console, Process) -> Int {
        println(7);
        return 0;
    }
}
```

Expected: prints `7`, exits 0. Actual: killed by SIGABRT; `--emit-llvm` shows
`call void @_C.m.print_int(i64 7)`. A 2026-10-18 build (before symbol mangling) emits
`call void @print_int(i64 7)` into the same user definition, so the defect predates the mangling
work; mangling neither caused nor fixed it.

## Cause

`Elab` builds the desugared calls as `CExpr.call "print_int" ...` (`Elab.lean`, the `println`
desugaring), a bare spelling. Every later pass resolves a call by its spelling, and the module's
own definition wins (`Lower`: a defined function is never intercepted as an intrinsic). The symbol
work binds a spelling the module's resolver gives to the runtime helper to its reserved
`_C$rt.` symbol (`CFnDef.foreignCalls`), but when the module itself defines `print_int` the
resolver gives the spelling to that definition, so a generated call and an explicit call to the
user's `print_int` are indistinguishable. Reserving the names is not an option: test programs
define `print_int` etc. deliberately (`print_int_basic.con`, `cap_basic.con`, ...).

## Structural cause

Declaration identity by spelled name ([structural class](STRUCTURAL_CLASSES.md) 1): a
compiler-generated call carries no callee identity, only a spelling, so it binds to whatever the
spelling resolves to at the call site. Bug 129 (a user `malloc` capturing the allocator call) is the
same class for the C runtime and was closed by giving the compiler's own C calls a foreign callee
(`SCallee.foreign`); this is the Concrete-runtime half.

## Structural owner

R-0492 (S5 `DefId`): desugared calls carry the runtime helper's identity from creation through
Core and SSA. The narrow repair under exit 0b: give Elab's generated calls a distinct callee
identity (a runtime-callee form in Core, like `SCallee.foreign` in SSA) that Check, Mono, Lower,
the interpreter and the proof extractor treat as the helper.

## Containment while open

`scripts/tests/check_example_outputs.sh` (leg "open-bug reproducers", mode `signals`) requires the
binary to be killed by a signal; when the program prints 7 and exits 0, that leg fails until this
document, the corpus entry and the leg are updated together.
